reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space of dimension d. For every probability measure mu on E, reference point xstar and real sigma, if the squared distance to xstar is mu-integrable, then it is integrable under the law piSigma of X+sigma Z for independent X with law mu and standard centered Gaussian Z, and its piSigma integral equals its mu integral plus sigma^2 d. No positivity of sigma is required.
objects: E, mu, xstar, sigma, d and the Gaussian-smoothed law piSigma.
domains: Finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space; probability measures on E; sigma real.
quantifiers: Every probability mu, point xstar and real sigma satisfying the finite position second moment premise.
assumptions: mu is a probability law and x maps to norm(x-xstar)^2 is mu-integrable.
conclusion: The same observable is piSigma-integrable and its integral is exactly the original integral plus sigma^2 d.
scopes: Measure-level independent Gaussian smoothing only; no dynamics, stationarity, contraction, history or cost theorem.
constant_dependencies: The additive correction is exactly sigma^2 times the real dimension and has no other dependence.
